# Implementation Plan: codex raw-session Happy autoconnect (native Rust `codex-happy`)

## Revision (operator refinements 2026-06-21)

Three operator refinements were folded into this plan via surgical edits (the Phase-4
review block and ralph-meta header are preserved):

1. **Auto-onboard (reframes "not configured").** When the feature is ENABLED but Happy is
   not yet configured (no `~/.happy` credentials), `codex` now **self-onboards** instead of
   dead-ending to silent vanilla. Source check (`packages/happy-cli/src/ui/auth.ts`
   `doAuth`/`authAndSetupMachineIfNeeded`; `api/auth.ts` is a dead shim) confirms the fork
   has **no server-side account-creation endpoint** — identity = GitHub OAuth token +
   Dev-Tunnels ownership, and the E2EE identity is a **locally-generated** keypair
   (`tweetnacl.box.keyPair()` → `~/.happy/access.key`). **Self-onboard verdict: the
   identity/credential establishment is fully codex-native** — codex can, by itself, run the
   GitHub device flow (it already does for Copilot, `codex-copilot/src/auth.rs`), generate the
   E2EE keypair (US-002 crypto), write `~/.happy/profile.json` (a `GET api.github.com/user`),
   and seed `machineId`. Two pre-existing boundaries remain that are **identical to
   `happy codex`'s own first run** (NOT codex-self-onboard blockers): **(P1)** a one-time
   **mobile pairing** — the phone does its own GitHub login + `POST /pair/complete` (inherent
   to the 2nd device of an E2EE pair; codex surfaces the affordance, the human completes it),
   and **(P2)** a **reachable happy-server + a hosted Dev Tunnel** for cross-device reach
   (daemon/`tunnelManager.ts` infra, machine-scope, deferred-to-D). So fallback-to-vanilla now
   narrows to: feature OFF, the user aborts the GitHub login, or the server is genuinely
   unreachable/offline.
2. **Default-OFF.** The feature ships **disabled** (was default-on). Users opt in via ANY of:
   `/experimental`, `~/.codex-copilot/config.toml`, a startup flag
   (`-c features.remote_session=true` / `--enable remote_session`), or the new per-session
   `/remote on` command (refinement 3). Default-off also resolves the first-run-surprise
   concern (a brand-new user gets plain vanilla codex until they opt in).
3. **Per-session `/remote` command.** A new TUI slash command **`/remote`** (args `on`/`off`)
   enables/disables the feature mid-session ON TOP OF the surfaces above. `/remote on` flips
   the feature on + attaches the `codex-happy` client (self-onboarding per #1 if needed);
   `/remote off` flips it off + cleanly detaches the client without killing the codex session.
   Mechanism is codex's existing live `set_feature_enabled` toggle
   (`tui/src/chatwidget/settings.rs:69` — the same path `/experimental` drives for
   `UserMessageStyling`), registered in the `SlashCommand` enum (`tui/src/slash_command.rs`).

**Chosen identifiers (surfaced for operator confirmation at review):** feature key
**`remote_session`** (`Feature::RemoteSession`) — renamed from the original
`features.happy_autoconnect` everywhere in these deliverables; command **`/remote on|off`**.
Deliberately distinct from the force-disabled `remote_control` (the retired ChatGPT enrollment
— patch-surface Inv 8/9): `_session` (your codex session is reachable from your phone) vs
`_control` (the enrollment we force-off). **No self-onboard blocker was found** that needs an
operator decision before implementation.

## Overview

Make a raw `codex` invocation of our fork binary behave **exactly like `happy codex`** at the
session level — appears on the Happy mobile session tree within seconds, streams its conversation
E2EE, and is **fully bidirectionally controllable from mobile** (send turns; exec + patch approvals
route to the phone and the mobile decision drives the live session; interrupt/stop work) — with **no
happy-cli process at runtime**. codex-rs speaks the Happy wire protocol directly to happy-server
(cross-machine only via Microsoft Dev Tunnels). The feature ships **default-OFF**; once the user
opts in (`/experimental`, `~/.codex-copilot/config.toml`, `-c features.remote_session=true` /
`--enable remote_session`, or the new `/remote on` command) raw `codex` connects when Happy creds
are present. **If the feature is enabled but Happy is not yet configured (no `~/.happy`
credentials), codex self-onboards** — it establishes the necessary parts natively (GitHub
device-flow login + a locally-generated E2EE identity keypair + `~/.happy/profile.json` +
machineId) and then connects, behaving like `happy codex`'s first run (a one-time mobile pairing
on the phone still completes the E2EE pair). Raw `codex` falls back to plain vanilla codex (never
broken) ONLY when the feature is off, the user aborts the GitHub login, or the server is genuinely
unreachable/offline. An explicit `happy codex` (and a
`codex app-server` child it spawns) must NOT double-wrap. Machine-level features (presence,
spawn-from-mobile, fork-into-worktree, keepalive) are explicitly OUT of v1 scope.

This is **Direction B** from the brainstorm (a fork-exclusive overlay crate
`codex/codex-rs-overlay/codex-happy` porting the Happy *protocol* client to Rust), driven through a
**bounded, registered, rebase-gated upstream-canonical control seam at the codex in-process
app-server boundary**. The Phase-0 spike already returned a **GO** verdict with port-effort **L**:
the crypto is proven byte-compatible bidirectionally vs `encryption.ts`, the `POST /v1/sessions` +
Socket.IO contract is satisfiable with no happy-server changes, and the seam came in **bounded**
(measured ~88 add / 1 del across 2 files; ~6-8 conflict-creating lines at one chokepoint). This is a
**codex-submodule-targeted plan**: implementation is a codex-submodule effort using the fork's
two-commit submodule flow (commit inside `codex/`, then bump the codexu pointer).

- **Crypto fidelity caveat (must verify, do NOT "fix"):** `api.ts` computes a `dataEncryptionKey` for dataKey

  `api.ts`'s ACTUAL on-the-wire behavior byte-for-byte (verify what is really sent), not an idealized version
  — getting this wrong silently breaks session decryptability on mobile. Pinned to US-003 + Open Questions.

**Crypto crate set (spike-proven byte-compatible)** — from `cryptocompat/Cargo.toml`: `sha2` 0.10,
`crypto_box` 0.9 (`std`), `xsalsa20poly1305` 0.9, `aes-gcm` 0.10, `ed25519-dalek` 2, `hex` 0.4. The X25519/
SalsaBox sealed-box (with the libsodium `sha512(seed)[0:32]` pubkey quirk and the custom
ephPub‖nonce‖SalsaBox bundle), legacy secretbox, AES-256-GCM dataKey bundle (`0‖nonce12‖ct‖tag16`), and
Ed25519 auth challenge all replicate exactly. **Reuse `cryptocompat/src/main.rs` + `crosscheck.mts` as the
basis for the crate's encryption module AND as KAT fixtures.**

### Technical Constraints
- **The launcher cannot host a session-lifetime client** (`exec()`s codex-core and exits). The in-core
  `codex-happy` client must be attached inside codex-core's runtime at session start — `tui/src/app.rs`,
  after `app_server` is constructed and before the main loop (~1137-1204), via
  `codex_happy::attach(tap_rx, request_handle)`. The launcher's job is only to pass creds/feature state
  through env/config that codex-core reads at session start.
- **`core/src/session/mod.rs` `Codex { tx_sub, rx_event }`** — `rx_event` is single-consumer `pub(crate)`,
  so an overlay crate cannot subscribe to it. This is exactly why the seam is the app-server boundary.
- **The seam may be even smaller than the spike measured.** At the spike tree (0.141 HEAD 50ac507c) the
  cloneable handle lacked `resolve_server_request`/`reject_server_request`, so the spike ADDED them. In the
  CURRENT tree the researcher found `resolve_server_request` at `app-server-client/src/lib.rs:684-709` +
  enum dispatch 884-892 and `reject_server_request` at 711-737 + 895-903, AND an existing approval-resolve
  bridge at `tui/src/app_server_session.rs:1136-1141`. So the only *guaranteed* upstream modification is the
  outbound tee at `app.rs:1202-1210` + the `happy_tap` field + the attach call. **Impl must verify at build
  time whether the resolve/reject methods are already on the cloneable handle; add them additively only if
  missing** (per `probe-a-seam.diff`).
- **Dependency audit sizing:** `crypto_box`, `ed25519-dalek`, `reqwest`, `sha2`, `aes-gcm`, `x25519-dalek`
  are ALREADY in the patched workspace (Cargo.toml 307/319/384/405/300, Cargo.lock 200/15585). **Only
  `xsalsa20poly1305` + `rust-socketio` are net-new audited surface.**
- **Idempotency facts:** `HAPPY_CURRENT_SESSION_ID` is defined `packages/happy-cli/src/utils/envNames.ts:1-4`,
  set on the codex child env at `src/codex/runCodex.ts:943-953`, and checked at
  `src/codex/codexAppServerClient.ts:1003-1023`. Codex subcommand dispatch is `cli/src/main.rs:627-645`
  (+ app-server parse 2243-2276). Rule: suppress native autoconnect if `HAPPY_CURRENT_SESSION_ID` is set OR
  subcommand is `app-server`.
- **Patch-surface registration:** `codex/docs/implementation/patch-surface.md` §4 (network egress) 63-85,
  §14 invariant-to-test table at 769 (rows like `| 10 | Launcher provider flags emit
  features.remote_control=false. | grep | scripts/audit_invariants.sh ... |`), §15 at 1356. Network audit:
  `codex/scripts/audit_network_calls.sh` (`KNOWN_PATCH_FILES` 34-48, `OVERLAY_KNOWN_PATCH_FILES` 69-74,
  `ENDPOINT_PATTERNS` 90-116, `EXCLUDED_FILES` 118-197). The runtime allowlist is at the confirmed canonical
  path `codex/scripts/runtime_audit_allowlist.txt` (the researcher Explore agent's "not found outside

## Approach

### Architecture
A new overlay crate `codex/codex-rs-overlay/codex-happy` (zero upstream conflict surface) holds ALL Happy
logic: encryption, HTTP session creation, the Socket.IO `/v1/updates` client, auth, `@slopus/happy-wire`
serde structs, the codex-event ↔ Happy-envelope mapping, and the mobile ↔ `ClientRequest` mapping, plus the
`attach(tap_rx, request_handle)` orchestrator. The crate becomes a **second in-process app-server consumer**:
- **Outbound** (events → mobile): a ~3-line tee at the single `AppServerClient::next_event()` chokepoint
  (`tui/src/app.rs:1202-1210`) clones each `AppServerEvent` (it `#[derive(Clone)]`) into an mpsc sink the
  crate owns.
- **Inbound** (mobile → session): the already-cloneable `AppServerRequestHandle` issues
  `ClientRequest::TurnStart`/`TurnSteer`/`TurnInterrupt`; exec/patch approvals resolve via
  `resolve_server_request` (already present in-tree — codex review confirmed it + `reject_server_request`
  exist; route through the existing `app_server_session.rs:1136-1141` bridge when possible). `tui/src/app_command.rs`
  (`AppCommand::{UserTurn, ExecApproval, PatchApproval, Interrupt, Shutdown}`) + `core/src/session/handlers.rs`
  (`Op::{UserInput, Interrupt, ExecApproval, PatchApproval, Shutdown}`) are the behavioral oracle / documented
  fallback inbound path if the request-handle proves insufficient.
- **Tap channel policy (no TUI backpressure):** the outbound tap is an `UnboundedSender<AppServerEvent>` (as in
  the spike) so it NEVER blocks or hangs the TUI event loop; the overlay owns all buffering, reconnect, and
  drop policy on its side. Lossless transcript events (assistant deltas/completions) must reach mobile or be
  re-fetched on reconnect; only genuinely droppable events may be dropped under sustained slow-mobile/socket
  backpressure. US-005 must specify this policy and test lossless assistant deltas/completions under a slow
  mobile / socket reconnect.
- **Stop/interrupt vs kill semantics:** mobile *interrupt* → `TurnInterrupt`. Mobile *stop/kill* must map
  explicitly to the in-process equivalents of happy-cli's `runCodex.ts` behavior (`permissionHandler.abortAll()`
  + `client.abortTurnWithFallback(...)` + `killSession` process termination). For a native in-process client
  there is no separate process to kill, so "stop" = abort the current turn (`TurnInterrupt`) + cancel pending
  approvals + (optionally) tear down the session; US-007 must define and test this abort-vs-kill mapping so the
  interrupt/stop acceptance criterion is actually satisfied.

The overlay attaches when the feature is enabled and the session is not already Happy-driven: if creds
are present it connects immediately; if the feature is enabled but creds are absent it first **self-onboards**
(background GitHub device-flow login + local E2EE identity establishment + `~/.happy/profile.json` + machineId,
per US-003) and then connects. With the feature OFF (the default), or when the user aborts the GitHub login,
or when the server is genuinely unreachable/offline, codex starts as plain vanilla codex with no added startup
hang/prompt/error. The self-onboard's interactive GitHub device-flow prompt is surfaced non-blockingly and never
blocks the first codex prompt.

### Implementation Strategy
Front-load risk; keep the overlay crate independently buildable/testable (everything through the socket
client is unit-testable without the seam). Ordered work:
1. **Early live happy-server round-trip de-risk** — resolve the deployed auth-mode/cap-file detail before the
   deep port (the one thing the spike could not execute end-to-end).
2. **Crate scaffold + encryption module** — port `encryption.ts` byte-for-byte (reuse `cryptocompat`).
3. **`getOrCreateSession` (POST /v1/sessions, dataKey + legacy) + auth module** (GitHub device flow + Dev
   Tunnels connect token; `~/.happy` cred read).
4. **Socket.IO `/v1/updates` client + happy-wire serde structs** — seq-ordered updates, CAS metadata/state,
   message-consumption acks, session-alive keepalive, smart reconnect, rpc handling (the behavior-parity port).
5. **Bounded upstream-canonical control seam + build/feature wiring** — the tee + `happy_tap` field (+ additive
   handle methods only if missing); **register `codex-happy` in `tui/Cargo.toml`** (else `cargo check` fails)
   and the root workspace `Cargo.toml`; **register the `remote_session` experimental feature** in
   `features/src/lib.rs` + `features/src/tests.rs` (strict config rejects unknown `features.*` keys); all
   `// SANDBOX PATCH:` marked + patch-surface §14 rows + enforcing invariant tests. This MUST land before US-006.
6. **Launcher wiring + attach + idempotency + self-onboard + graceful fallback + opt-in (default-OFF)** (incl.
   Windows parity via the launcher's Windows spawn+wait branch — there is NO in-repo `codex.ps1`) — delivers
   "appears on tree + streams E2EE". Attach when the feature is enabled; self-onboard when creds are absent
   (US-003); the feature ships disabled and is opted into via `/experimental` / `~/.codex-copilot/config.toml` /
   `-c features.remote_session=true` (`--enable remote_session`) / the `/remote` command.
7. **Full bidirectional control** — turns + exec/patch approval routing + interrupt/stop, with double-answer
   coordination.
8. **Network-audit registration + happy-wire drift guard** — allowlist the new egress + the 2 net-new deps;
   pin the wire schema with a failing-on-drift guard.
9. **Per-session `/remote on|off` slash command** — register `SlashCommand::Remote` (`tui/src/slash_command.rs`)
   + dispatch through the existing live `set_feature_enabled` toggle (`tui/src/chatwidget/settings.rs:69`, the
   `UserMessageStyling` precedent): `/remote on` flips `remote_session` on + attaches (self-onboarding if needed);
   `/remote off` flips it off + cleanly detaches the `codex-happy` client without killing the codex session.

## Scope

### In Scope
- The `codex-happy` overlay crate: encryption (5 spike-proven primitives + bundle layouts),
  `getOrCreateSession` (dataKey + legacy), Socket.IO `/v1/updates` client (seq-ordered updates, CAS
  metadata/state, message-consumption acks, session-alive keepalive, smart reconnect, rpc), auth (GitHub
  device flow + Dev Tunnels connect token), happy-wire serde structs.
- The bounded upstream-canonical control seam at the app-server boundary (event tee + inbound
  turn/interrupt/stop + approval resolve), each `// SANDBOX PATCH:`-marked + patch-surface §14/§15 registered
  + an enforcing test.
- Launcher wiring (attach when the feature is enabled), idempotency (no double-wrap when
  `HAPPY_CURRENT_SESSION_ID` set OR subcommand is `app-server`), graceful silent fallback (feature off / user
  aborts GitHub login / server unreachable / offline → vanilla codex within a startup-latency budget),
  opt-in/config: the feature ships **default-OFF** and is enabled via ANY of `/experimental`,
  `~/.codex-copilot/config.toml`, a startup flag (`-c features.remote_session=true` / `--enable remote_session`),
  or the `/remote` command; Windows parity (launcher spawn+wait branch, no in-repo `codex.ps1`).
- **Auto-onboard:** when the feature is enabled but Happy is not yet configured (no `~/.happy` creds), codex
  self-establishes the codex-native parts — GitHub device-flow login, a locally-generated E2EE identity keypair
  (`~/.happy/access.key`), `~/.happy/profile.json`, and `machineId` — then connects (US-003). The one-time mobile
  pairing (phone-side GitHub login + `POST /pair/complete`) and the reachable-server/hosted-tunnel infra remain
  the same prerequisites `happy codex`'s own first run has (the latter is machine-scope, deferred-to-D).
- **Per-session enable/disable command `/remote` (`on`/`off`):** a dedicated TUI slash command that live-toggles
  `remote_session` mid-session (attach + self-onboard on `on`; clean detach on `off`), on top of the opt-in surfaces above.
- Full mobile bidirectional control: send turns; exec + patch approvals route to mobile and the mobile
  decision drives the live session; interrupt/stop cancel the live turn; approval double-answer coordination.
- Network-audit registration (happy-server + Dev-Tunnels egress + the 2 net-new deps) in
  `audit_network_calls.sh` + runtime audit allowlist + patch-surface §4, with justification.
- `@slopus/happy-wire` drift guard (pin + a test failing when the TS schema advances without a Rust update).
- An EARLY de-risk story: the live happy-server round-trip (resolve tunnel-auth/cap-file) before the deep port.

### Out of Scope
- Machine-level parity: machine presence, spawn-from-mobile, fork-into-worktree, worktree spawns, daemon
  keepalive (`api/apiMachine.ts`). Deferred to a happy-cli daemon (direction D) fast-follow.
- Directions A (launcher delegation into `happy codex`), C (permanent bridge sidecar), D (happy-cli owns the
  wire) as the primary design — B is chosen; A/D remain only as transitional safety valves / the fallback.
- happy-server protocol/schema changes — v1 must round-trip the existing server contract.
- Cross-machine transport changes — Dev Tunnels remain the sole cross-machine data path; never bind to
  non-loopback.
- The prior read-only daemon-mirror fallback is NOT built here (retained separately as the degraded fallback);
  the fallback this plan implements is silent vanilla codex (feature off / GitHub login aborted / server
  unreachable / offline). Hosting a cross-device Dev Tunnel and standing up the embedded happy-server are
  daemon/infra concerns (machine-scope, deferred-to-D); the self-onboard establishes only the codex-native
  identity/credential parts, not the tunnel/server infra.

## Risk Areas
1. **NEW audited network egress inside codex-core (highest residual).** The fork's whole purpose is
   non-Copilot egress suppression. happy-server + Dev Tunnels + the 2 net-new deps become allowlisted
   destinations requiring `audit_network_calls.sh` + runtime allowlist + patch-surface §4 registration with
   justification. Mitigation: register precisely (loopback-only locally, Dev-Tunnels-only cross-machine),
   keep all egress call sites in the overlay crate, justify in §4. This is the strongest argument that ever
   favored D; carry it explicitly.
2. **E2EE key-ownership shift into the audited binary.** codex reads `~/.happy` creds and owns per-session
   data keys (replacing the daemon-sole-holder); with self-onboard (US-003) it also **generates** the account
   E2EE identity keypair and writes `~/.happy/access.key`/`profile.json`. Same user/machine trust boundary (the codex
   child already inherits all `HAPPY_*` env today), but key material is now both created and held by the
   network-audited binary — call out in §4.
3. **Approval double-answer.** The local TUI ALSO receives the approval `ServerRequest` and renders its own
   UI. Mitigation: dedup via app-server request-id (first resolve wins — verify) OR suppress the local
   approval UI when Happy is attached. A handful of lines; pick one and test both branches.
4. **Perpetual `@slopus/happy-wire` two-implementation drift tax.** A Rust Socket.IO + NaCl-compatible crypto
   + AES-GCM dataKey + Ed25519 + wire-schema + metadata-CAS client must stay in lockstep with the evolving TS
   package. Mitigation: pin the in-repo wire schema + a CI drift guard that fails on un-mirrored schema advance.
5. **Startup-latency / fallback budget.** Feature-off, GitHub-login-aborted, server-unreachable, and offline must
   all be silent vanilla codex — no hang, no blocking prompt, no error. (Feature-ON + no-creds is NOT a fallback —
   it self-onboards, with the GitHub device-flow prompt surfaced non-blockingly.) Mitigation: bounded creds-probe +
   connect/self-onboard timeout; attach/onboard failures degrade silently; define the budget as an acceptance
   criterion (see Open Questions for the exact ms).
6. **Windows `codex.ps1` parity.** The Windows launcher path must carry identical behavior (no hang/prompt on
   plain `codex`). Mitigation: explicit Windows test in US-006.
7. **Live-server auth-mode/cap-file uncertainty.** The running `:3005` listener is in tunnel-auth mode and the
   LocalSystem service reads its cap file from the service profile, not the user's `~/.happy`. This blocked
   the spike's live POST. Mitigation: the EARLY de-risk story (US-001) resolves it cheaply before the deep port.
8. **Rebase drift of the seam.** The seam targets upstream-canonical files that rebase. Mitigation: keep the
   conflict-creating surface to the single tee chokepoint; register in patch-surface §14 with an enforcing
   test so a rebase that moves the chokepoint fails loudly.
9. **Crypto/wire fidelity vs idealized behavior.** The Rust client must replicate `api.ts`/`apiSession.ts`
   on-the-wire behavior byte-for-byte, including quirks (e.g. the `dataEncryptionKey: null` POST flagged by
   codex research) — not a "cleaned up" version. Mitigation: instrument/inspect the real TS calls in US-003/004,
   generate KAT fixtures from the actual TS output, and assert against them; the drift guard (US-008) keeps
   them honest over time.

## Acceptance Criteria
(Mirrors the brainstorm Criteria, with concrete measurable thresholds promoted from Open Questions; these are
the ship gates. Thresholds marked [tune] are starting targets the implementer may adjust with justification and
an asserting test.)
- With Happy creds present and the feature enabled, a raw `codex` start surfaces a new Happy server session on
  the mobile tree **within ≤5 s [tune]** of session start, NOT marked read-only, with codex-flavor metadata.
- With the feature enabled but **no `~/.happy` creds**, a raw `codex` start **self-onboards** the codex-native
  identity (GitHub device-flow login → locally-generated E2EE keypair `~/.happy/access.key` → `~/.happy/profile.json`
  → `machineId`) and THEN surfaces a session on the mobile tree, with no server-side account-creation step required.
  The GitHub device-flow prompt is surfaced non-blockingly (never blocks the first codex prompt); if the user
  declines/aborts it or the server is unreachable, codex degrades to vanilla. The one-time phone-side pairing
  (`POST /pair/complete`) and a reachable server/tunnel are the same prerequisites `happy codex`'s first run has.
- From mobile: sending a turn drives the live raw codex session and its streamed output mirrors back E2EE; an
  exec approval AND a patch approval requested by codex route to mobile and the mobile decision is what the live
  session acts on; **interrupt** issued from mobile aborts the live turn so streamed output ceases **within ≤2 s
  [tune]** and codex reports the turn aborted; **stop/kill** maps to the abort-vs-kill semantics defined in
  US-007 (abort current turn + cancel pending approvals + optional session teardown) — not just the client view.
- **Smart reconnect is observable:** after a socket drop, the client reconnects and resumes within **≤10 s
  [tune]**, and any `update` seq gap is backfilled so no assistant delta/completion is permanently lost.
- No happy-cli process is running at any point during the raw `codex` session (verified by process inspection)
  for the session-level control path.
- Encryption is byte-compatible with happy-cli: a session created by the Rust client is fully
  readable/controllable from the existing mobile app; `dataKey` and `legacy` modes both round-trip. The
  `getOrCreateSession` request body matches what `api.ts` actually sends (incl. the `dataEncryptionKey` value
  — verify, do not "fix").
- Explicit `happy codex` (and a `codex app-server` child it spawns) does NOT auto-connect a second time —
  exactly one Happy session per intended session; no duplicates.
- The feature ships **default-OFF**: a fresh install with the feature unset behaves as plain vanilla codex; the
  feature is enabled by any of `/experimental`, `~/.codex-copilot/config.toml`, `-c features.remote_session=true`
  (`--enable remote_session`), or the `/remote on` command. Asserted by a test.
- The per-session **`/remote` command** toggles the live session: `/remote on` (mid-session) flips `remote_session`
  on and attaches the `codex-happy` client (self-onboarding if creds are absent) so the session appears on the
  mobile tree; `/remote off` flips it off and cleanly detaches the client (Happy session/sync stops) WITHOUT
  killing the codex session. Both directions are tested (TUI integration test driving the live `set_feature_enabled` path).
- With the feature **OFF (the default)**, raw `codex` is byte-for-byte plain vanilla codex — the **≤300 ms [tune]
  added latency over the vanilla baseline** is not even incurred (no probe runs), no auth prompt, no error. With the
  feature ON but the connect/self-onboard cannot complete (user declines the GitHub login, or the server is
  unreachable/offline), raw `codex` still reaches the interactive prompt within **≤300 ms [tune] added latency over the
  vanilla baseline**, no blocking auth prompt, no error; the connect/self-onboard attempt is fully background and never
  blocks the first prompt. Identical on the Windows launcher path.
- The upstream-canonical seam + build/feature wiring is bounded, each modified line `// SANDBOX PATCH:`-marked
  and registered in patch-surface §14/§15 with an enforcing test/guard; `tui/Cargo.toml` declares the dep and
  `remote_session` is registered in `features/src/lib.rs`; `cargo check --workspace` passes; the network audit
  passes with the new egress + overlay egress files allowlisted (each carrying a `// SANDBOX PATCH:` marker) + justified.
- A drift guard fails CI when the pinned in-repo `@slopus/happy-wire` schema (`packages/happy-wire/src/`) advances
  without a matching `codex-happy` Rust update.

## Preliminary Story Decomposition
- **US-001** Live happy-server round-trip de-risk (EARLY GATE): resolve deployed auth-mode/cap-file; produce a
  working authenticated request path for the crate.
- **US-002** `codex-happy` crate scaffold + encryption module (reuse `cryptocompat`; KAT vs `encryption.ts`).
- **US-003** `getOrCreateSession` (POST /v1/sessions, dataKey + legacy) + auth/onboarding module (GitHub device
  flow + Dev Tunnels token; `~/.happy` cred read). Capture + replicate `api.ts`'s actual on-the-wire body (incl. the
  `dataEncryptionKey: null` quirk — verify, do not "fix"). **Self-onboard:** when the feature is enabled but
  `~/.happy` creds are absent, establish the codex-native identity — run the GitHub device flow (mirror
  `ui/auth.ts doAuth`/`auth/githubDeviceFlow.ts`; codex already has the device-flow shape in
  `codex-copilot/src/auth.rs`), generate the E2EE keypair locally (`tweetnacl.box.keyPair()` equivalent → write
  `~/.happy/access.key` dataKey creds), write `~/.happy/profile.json` (`GET api.github.com/user`), and seed
  `machineId` — then create the session. No server-side account-creation call exists; the one-time mobile pairing
  and a reachable server/tunnel stay as the same prerequisites `happy codex`'s first run has.
- **US-004** Socket.IO `/v1/updates` client + happy-wire serde structs from `packages/happy-wire/src/` (seq
  updates, CAS, message-consumption acks, session-alive keepalive, smart reconnect + seq-gap backfill, rpc).
- **US-005** Bounded upstream-canonical control seam + build/feature wiring: the tee + `happy_tap` `UnboundedSender`
  (never backpressures the TUI) + additive handle methods only if missing; **`tui/Cargo.toml` dep on `codex-happy`**;
  root `Cargo.toml` member/dep; **register `remote_session` in `features/src/lib.rs` + `features/src/tests.rs`**
  (strict config rejects unknown feature keys); `// SANDBOX PATCH:` + patch-surface §14 rows + enforcing tests
  (incl. a lossless-transcript test under slow-mobile/reconnect). MUST precede US-006.
- **US-006** Launcher wiring + attach + self-onboard (call US-003's onboarding when the feature is enabled but
  creds are absent) + idempotency (`HAPPY_CURRENT_SESSION_ID` / `app-server` subcommand) + graceful silent
  fallback (feature off / GitHub login aborted / server unreachable / offline) + opt-in **default-OFF**
  (`/experimental` + `~/.codex-copilot/config.toml` + `-c features.remote_session=true` / `--enable remote_session`
  + env override) + Windows parity via the launcher Windows spawn+wait branch (no in-repo `codex.ps1`) —
  delivers "appears on tree + streams E2EE".
- **US-007** Full bidirectional control: turns (`TurnStart`/`TurnSteer`) + exec/patch approval routing
  (`resolve_server_request`) + interrupt (`TurnInterrupt`) + the explicit **abort-vs-killSession mapping** (mirror
  `runCodex.ts` `abortAll`/`abortTurnWithFallback`/`killSession`) + approval double-answer coordination.
- **US-008** Network-audit registration (egress + 2 net-new deps `xsalsa20poly1305`/`rust-socketio`; each overlay
  egress file `// SANDBOX PATCH:`-marked + listed in `OVERLAY_KNOWN_PATCH_FILES`) + `runtime_audit_allowlist.txt`
  + patch-surface §4 + `@slopus/happy-wire` drift guard.
- **US-009** Per-session `/remote on|off` slash command: register `SlashCommand::Remote` (`tui/src/slash_command.rs`)
  + dispatch through the existing live `set_feature_enabled` toggle (`tui/src/chatwidget/{slash_dispatch.rs,
  settings.rs:69}`, the `UserMessageStyling` precedent). `/remote on` → flip `remote_session` on + attach
  (self-onboard via US-003 if creds absent); `/remote off` → flip off + cleanly detach the `codex-happy` client
  (stop the Happy session/sync) without killing the codex session. Each modified upstream line `// SANDBOX PATCH:`-marked
  + a patch-surface §14 row + a TUI integration test covering both directions.

## Suggested Decomposition
Keep this section consistent with `suggested-decomposition.json`. Heavy serial dependencies dominate (the
overlay crate is internally sequential, and the integration stories depend on both the crate and the seam),
with two safe parallel windows. The upstream-canonical seam is the riskiest cluster — keep it isolated.

### Cluster: derisk-and-crypto
- Stories: US-001, US-002
- Phase: 1
- Depends on: None
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[]; exclusive=[throwaway probe/findings under `.ralph/investigations/…`,
  `codex/codex-rs-overlay/codex-happy/{Cargo.toml,src/encryption.rs,src/lib.rs}`,
  `codex/external/repos/codex-patched/codex-rs/Cargo.toml` (workspace member add)]; risk=low
- `execution_mode` rationale: US-001 is a throwaway/findings de-risk; US-002 scaffolds the crate + crypto.
  They touch disjoint footprints and can run in parallel. (US-002's crypto needs no live server; US-003 later
  consumes US-001's resolved auth.) Both edit the workspace `Cargo.toml` only additively, but to avoid a
  merge race on that one file, run US-002 as the writer and have US-001 avoid Cargo.toml.

### Cluster: protocol-client
- Stories: US-003, US-004
- Phase: 2
- Depends on: derisk-and-crypto
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[`codex-happy/src/lib.rs`]; exclusive=[`codex-happy/src/{api.rs,auth.rs,
  session.rs,wire.rs}`]; risk=low
- `execution_mode` rationale: Both extend the same new crate (shared `lib.rs` module wiring) so they serialize
  internally, but the whole cluster is disjoint from the upstream seam files and can run in parallel with the
  `seam` cluster.

### Cluster: seam
- Stories: US-005
- Phase: 2
- Depends on: None
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[`codex/external/repos/codex-patched/codex-rs/tui/src/app.rs` (also touched by
  US-006 attach), `patch-surface.md` (§14; §4 touched by US-008)]; exclusive=[`app-server-client/src/lib.rs`,
  `tui/Cargo.toml` (codex-happy dep), `features/src/lib.rs` + `features/src/tests.rs` (register
  `remote_session`), `codex-invariant-tests/tests/happy_seam_invariants.rs`]; risk=medium (upstream-canonical edit)
- `execution_mode` rationale: Disjoint from the overlay-crate `src/` files, so it can run in parallel with
  `protocol-client`. It does NOT edit the root workspace `Cargo.toml` (US-002 owns that membership add), so no
  conflict with `derisk-and-crypto`. It shares `app.rs` with US-006 (attach) and `patch-surface.md` with US-008,
  so those serialize after this cluster. **MUST complete before `integration`**: US-006 cannot compile the
  attach call until `tui/Cargo.toml` depends on `codex-happy` and `remote_session` is a known feature key.

### Cluster: integration
- Stories: US-006, US-007, US-009
- Phase: 3
- Depends on: protocol-client, seam
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[`tui/src/app.rs` (attach/detach — US-006 + US-009), `codex-happy/src/attach.rs`
  (attach + detach API — US-006/US-009)]; exclusive=[`codex-copilot-launcher/src/{main.rs,config.rs}` (US-006),
  `tui/src/slash_command.rs` + `tui/src/chatwidget/{slash_dispatch.rs,settings.rs}` (US-009 `/remote` command)];
  risk=medium
- `execution_mode` rationale: Needs both the crate (US-003/004) and the seam + build/feature wiring (US-005)
  present and compiling; US-007 builds directly on US-006's attach, so the two serialize within the cluster.
  US-009 (`/remote`) reuses US-006's attach + US-007's clean-detach/teardown semantics for its `on`/`off`
  side-effects and edits the same `codex-happy` attach surface + `tui/src/app.rs`, so it serializes after
  US-006/US-007 within this cluster. Windows parity rides the launcher's existing Windows spawn+wait branch
  (`main.rs:176-187`) — there is no in-repo `codex.ps1` file to edit.

### Cluster: audit-drift
- Stories: US-008
- Phase: 4
- Depends on: protocol-client, seam
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[`patch-surface.md` (§4 vs the seam's §14)]; exclusive=[
  `scripts/audit_network_calls.sh`, runtime audit allowlist, `codex-invariant-tests/tests/happy_wire_drift_guard.rs`];
  risk=low
- `execution_mode` rationale: The egress to allowlist exists only after US-003/004 add the call sites and
  US-005 lands the seam; it edits `patch-surface.md` §4 (a different section than the seam's §14) so it
  serializes after `seam` to avoid a doc merge race, but is otherwise disjoint from `integration` and may
  overlap it on non-`patch-surface.md` files at the implementer's discretion.

## Open Questions
- **Exact v1 promise** — confirmed session-level only (machine scope deferred). [Resolved by brainstorm.]
- **Fallback-latency budget** — the Acceptance Criteria now set concrete `[tune]` ship gates (feature-OFF = plain
  vanilla codex, no probe; feature-ON-but-can't-connect = ≤300 ms added over the vanilla baseline; the connect /
  self-onboard is fully background and never blocks the first prompt). These ARE the measurable gates — each must be
  asserted by a test; `[tune]` means the implementer may adjust the specific number with written justification, NOT
  that the gate is optional. US-001 (the live de-risk) refines the realistic connect timing before US-006 locks the
  asserted values.
- **Approval double-answer mechanism** — dedup-by-request-id vs suppress-local-UI is not yet decided; US-007
  must verify whether the app-server's request-id dedup makes the first `resolve` win (preferred) before
  committing to suppressing the local UI.
- **Config placement / default** — RESOLVED by operator refinement (2026-06-21): the feature ships **default-OFF**
  and is opted into via ANY of `/experimental`, `~/.codex-copilot/config.toml`, a startup flag
  (`-c features.remote_session=true` / `--enable remote_session`), or the new `/remote on` command. The feature key
  is **`remote_session`** (`Feature::RemoteSession`) — chosen to be non-colliding with the force-disabled
  `remote_control` (ChatGPT enrollment, patch-surface Inv 8/9); the command is **`/remote on|off`**. The chosen
  names are surfaced for operator confirmation at review (adjust freely); confirm the env-override name at impl.
- **Runtime audit allowlist location** — RESOLVED: the canonical allowlist is
  `codex/scripts/runtime_audit_allowlist.txt` (confirmed present). US-008 edits this file plus
  `audit_network_calls.sh` + patch-surface §4; verify the exact line format in-file at impl.
- **`dataEncryptionKey` on-the-wire shape (dataKey mode)** — codex research flagged that `api.ts` computes a
  `dataEncryptionKey` but appears to POST `dataEncryptionKey: null`. **Confirmed from source** (`api/api.ts:47-71`):
  the sealed key is computed but the body literally sends `dataEncryptionKey: null`. US-003 MUST replicate this exact
  on-the-wire shape in Rust; do not "correct" it. A wrong choice here silently breaks mobile decryptability.
- **Self-onboard scope (operator refinement 2026-06-21) — verdict: codex-native, no blocker.** Source check
  (`ui/auth.ts doAuth`/`authAndSetupMachineIfNeeded`, `persistence.ts`, server `auth.ts`/`accountRoutes.ts`/
  `pairRoutes.ts`, app `auth/pairing.ts`) confirms the fork has **no server-side account-creation endpoint** —
  identity = GitHub OAuth + Dev-Tunnels ownership, and the account E2EE identity is a **locally-generated** keypair.
  So codex can self-establish ALL of: GitHub token (device flow), the E2EE keypair, `profile.json`, and `machineId`
  with no mobile app and no server registration. Two pre-existing boundaries remain — identical to `happy codex`'s
  own first run, NOT codex-self-onboard blockers: **(P1)** the one-time mobile pairing (phone-side GitHub login +
  `POST /pair/complete`; inherent to the 2nd device of an E2EE pair), and **(P2)** a reachable happy-server + a hosted
  Dev Tunnel for cross-device reach (daemon/`tunnelManager.ts` infra, machine-scope, deferred-to-D). US-006 surfaces
  the GitHub-login affordance non-blockingly; it does NOT stand up the tunnel/server. Open sub-question for impl: how
  the mobile app obtains the per-session content key under dataKey mode + `dataEncryptionKey: null` (the pairing-time
  ECDH `mobileSharedSecret` in `pairRoutes.ts` vs the account keypair) — this is a protocol-port detail for US-003/004,
  not an onboarding blocker; the spike already asserts a Rust-created session is mobile-decryptable.
- **Key-ownership / audited-egress acceptability** — accepted as a known cost per the brainstorm; surfaced in
  §4 justification, not re-litigated here.
- **Drift-tax acceptability** — accepted; mitigated by the US-008 drift guard.
- **Research-tooling note (this box)** — codex-exec research completed (slowly) and its insights are folded in;
  copilot-exec research/review fail here on the `.xwin-cache` read-only snapshot budget. The plan is grounded
  in two Explore briefs + codex research + the authoritative spike/brainstorm; no planning gap resulted.
  Phase-4 copilot review is unavailable on this box — codex + Claude are the review safety net.
